source.title: Neural correlates of inner speech and auditory verbal hallucinations: a critical review and theoretical integration

confidence_rationale: Provides the explicit Vygotskian internalisation MECHANISM that the compression ladder (MECH-381) needs: inner speech develops through a transition between EXPANDED (full, external-like, dialogic) and CONDENSED (abbreviated, covert) forms, and the neural-correlates literature is read through that lens (low verbal-self-monitoring tasks like reciting in inner speech vs high VSM tasks like auditory verbal imagery dissociate in temporal-lobe activation). The compression-and-condensation account is the closest mechanistic statement of MECH-381's externalise->internalise axis. Confidence is moderate because the paper's primary explanatory target is auditory verbal hallucinations (a pathology of mis-attributed inner speech), so the mapping to a healthy REE control surface runs through a clinical model, and the neural evidence is correlational.
failure_signatures: The condensed/expanded framework is a theoretical integration of mixed and partly inconsistent neuroimaging findings, not a settled mechanism -- the authors themselves flag that prior studies rested on 'unexamined assumptions about the form and developmental significance of inner speech'.

The paper's account of WHEN inner speech is mis-attributed (AVHs arise from abnormalities in the condensed<->expanded transition) implies the compression ladder has a failure mode REE has not modelled: a poorly tagged self-generated control signal can be experienced as external/other, i.e. the ladder is not automatically safe.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Inner speech is internalised external dialogue (Vygotsky) and exists along a continuum from EXPANDED (full sentence-like, retaining the turn-taking structure of social dialogue) to CONDENSED (abbreviated, semantic, covert) forms. The neural-correlates literature is coherent if read through this developmental lens: tasks with low verbal-self-monitoring demands vs high demands dissociate in middle/superior temporal gyrus engagement. Auditory verbal hallucinations are reframed as a disorder of the transition between condensed and expanded dialogic inner speech, explaining their other-voice, command-like quality.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds MECH-381's compression axis with an explicit mechanism: the SAME regulatory content is carried first in expanded (external-like) form and later in condensed (covert) form, and the transition between them is the unit of compression. Reinforces MECH-380's claim that the external phase is a genuine control/monitoring surface (high-VSM tasks recruit distinct circuitry). The dialogic structure also speaks to MECH-382's distancing operator: inner speech can carry more than one perspective.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's engine is a clinical model of hallucination, not a developmental-control account of a healthy agent; the transfer to a non-clinical, non-linguistic REE control surface is two steps removed. The neural dissociations are correlational and were partly contested even at publication.
mapping.source_context: Critical review integrating neuroimaging/neurophysiology of inner speech in healthy adults and remitted AVH-experiencers, framed by a Vygotskian developmental theory; human only.

confidence_components.notes: Influential and well-cited but a theoretical integration of mixed evidence, and clinically framed -- source quality good not excellent. Mapping fidelity moderate: the condensed/expanded transition is the best available statement of MECH-381's compression mechanism, but it arrives via an AVH model. Transfer risk high (clinical + linguistic -> non-clinical non-linguistic substrate).
